Description: Data discovery, environment setup, profiling, and groundwork for all subsequent work. Includes LLM tooling provisioning, schema profiling across all sources (JUNO, Holocentric, ALEX, Alfabet, linkages), prompt library setup, and audit trail framework implementation.

Find the payment processes (step 2), the JUNO payment controls (step 4), the bespoke controls (step 5), and run the convergence loop (step 6). Includes deterministic inclusion paths, embedding-based similarity paths, fuzzy matching infrastructure, and SME queue construction.

Classify Payment Nature on processes (step 3), Payment Nature on controls (step 7), Master Controls CT1–CT28 (step 8), and lifecycle stage A–G (step 9). All LLM-driven with structured JSON outputs, confidence scoring, and rationale grounding.

Compose all upstream outputs into the master analytical bridge table (step 10). Single SAS dataset with process × control × CT × Payment Nature × lifecycle stage schema. Indexed for query performance. All step 11 outputs query this table.

Produce the eight outputs in step 11: coverage heatmaps (three cuts), strengthen view, duplicates with best of breed, governance controls misclassified, gap register (six types), JUNO registration backlog, obligations coverage, monitoring baseline. Pure SAS queries over the bridge table.

SME-led validation gates across all LLM-driven steps (2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 9). SMEs from Line 1 Risk and Compliance construct golden sets and adjudicate disagreements. Independent LRM verifies at scale; disagreements queue to SME. Requires Human Review queue is SME-owned. Audit trail captured per AI decision with prompt hash, model ID, timestamp, input hash, raw response.

Summary: Build the audit trail capture framework
Description: Implement the audit trail records table per runbook specification. Every LLM call writes: prompt_version_hash (from prompt_versions.json), model_id (e.g., 'claude-sonnet-4-20250514'), run_timestamp (ISO8601), input_snapshot_hash (SHA-256 of concatenated input text fields to detect if source data changed between runs), raw_response (model output before parsing), parsed_result (structured JSON after schema validation), pass_number (for steps 2 & 4 convergence loop only, null for other steps), sme_override (if SME revises LLM decision, record override with SME name + timestamp + rationale; original LLM result preserved). Framework is reusable across all LLM steps. Demonstrate re-run capability: given audit record, reproduce exact same call with same inputs and compare outputs (deterministic if prompt and input unchanged; model version drift acceptable as long as documented).
Acceptance Criteria:

Audit trail table schema defined in 05_audit_trail/ with SAS dataset template: fields = prompt_version_hash (CHAR 64), model_id (CHAR 100), run_timestamp (DATETIME), input_snapshot_hash (CHAR 64), raw_response (TEXT), parsed_result (TEXT JSON), pass_number (INT nullable), sme_override (TEXT nullable), confidence (CHAR 10), requires_sme_flag (BOOL)

Audit logger implemented in 02_code/python/llm_orchestration/audit_logger.py with functions: log_llm_call(step_name, item_id, prompt_hash, model_id, input_dict, raw_response, parsed_json, pass_num=None), compute_input_hash(input_dict), load_prompt_hash(prompt_filename); test with single call to step 3 Payment Nature prompt on sample process

Re-run demonstration: select one audit record from test call, extract prompt_hash + input_snapshot_hash, re-issue LLM call with same prompt version and input, compare raw_response (may differ due to model non-determinism) and parsed_result (should be semantically equivalent; flag if classification changed); document re-run test result in 00_documentation/audit_trail_rerun_test.md
4. Framework integration: all LLM scripts (step02_pp6_embedding.py, step03_payment_nature_classify.py, etc.) include audit_logger.log_llm_call() after every model invocation before proceeding to next item

Summary: Implement step 2 deterministic inclusion paths (PP1 PP2 PP3 PP5)
Description: Build the four deterministic Holocentric inclusion paths in parallel. PP1 hierarchy: process sits under known payments L2/L3 family (hardcoded list: 'Payments Processing', 'Fraud Management', 'Customer Payments', etc.; SQL WHERE clause on l2_process_name or l3_activity_name). PP2 value stream: process belongs to payments-relevant value stream (hardcoded list: 'Request to Payment', 'Fraud Detect to Correct', 'Payment Exceptions to Resolution'; SQL WHERE on value_stream_name). PP3 application linkage: process references payment-relevant application via Holocentric.applications → Alfabet (join to payment_relevant_apps.csv from PRS-5). PP5 keyword: process name or step description contains controlled payment terms (SAS regex: 'payment|payor|payee|remittance|settlement|clearing|BPAY|NPP|BECS|RTGS|direct.?debit|direct.?credit' case-insensitive; apply to process_name + concatenated step_descriptions). Output first-pass payment process register with all paths fired recorded, primary path (by confidence hierarchy PP1 > PP2 > PP4 > PP3 > PP5 > PP6), and confidence rollup (High if ≥2 paths including ≥1 of PP1/PP2/PP4, Medium if exactly one PP1/PP2/PP4 or PP3 alone, Low if only PP5 or PP6). Audit log every Holocentric process with paths evaluated and decision.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Four deterministic paths execute against full Holocentric universe (run 02_code/sas/step02_process_inclusion.sas deterministic section): PP1 SQL filter on l2_process_name IN ('Payments Processing', 'Fraud Management', 'Customer Payments', 'Transaction Monitoring', 'Payment Operations', 'Clearing and Settlement') OR l3_activity_name LIKE '%payment%' OR '%settlement%', PP2 SQL filter on value_stream_name IN ('Request to Payment', 'Fraud Detect to Correct', 'Payment Exceptions to Resolution', 'Customer Onboarding to Offboarding'), PP3 join Holocentric.applications to payment_relevant_apps.csv (from PRS-5) via Application_ID, PP5 regex on process_name and step_descriptions (concatenate all step_description per process with '|' delimiter; apply regex; flag if match found)

Output dataset created: 03_data/intermediate/step02_payment_process_register.sas7bdat with schema: process_id, process_name, l2_parent, value_stream, applications (array), pp1_fired (BOOL), pp2_fired (BOOL), pp3_fired (BOOL), pp4_fired (BOOL initially NULL; populated in step 6), pp5_fired (BOOL), pp6_fired (BOOL initially NULL), primary_path (CHAR 10 = PP1/PP2/PP3/PP4/PP5/PP6 based on hierarchy), confidence_rollup (CHAR 10 = High/Medium/Low per runbook formula)
3. Audit log created: 05_audit_trail/audit_trail_step02_deterministic.csv with every Holocentric process (even excluded ones): process_id, pp1_result, pp2_result, pp3_result, pp5_result, inclusion_decision (Included/Excluded), confidence, primary_path, reason_if_excluded

Summary: Implement step 4 deterministic inclusion paths (P1 P3 P4 P5)
Description: Build the four deterministic JUNO control inclusion paths via Teradata SQL pass-through. P1 taxonomy tag: control's risk_library_id IN ('7.4.1', '7.4.2', ..., '7.4.x' all Payments risk library tags; get exhaustive list from JUNO taxonomy table). P3 obligation linkage: control linked to payments obligation (join linkage_ctrl_oblig to obligations where obligation source IN ('NPP', 'BECS', 'RBA', 'ePayments Code', 'AUSTRAC', 'Payment Services Act') via Teradata SQL). P4 incident/issue linkage: control linked to payments-classified incident or issue (join linkage_ctrl_incident and linkage_ctrl_issue to incidents/issues where incident/issue is linked to 7.4.x controls or payment processes; iterative definition resolved in step 6). P5 keyword: control name or description contains controlled payment terms (same regex as PP5: 'payment|payor|payee|remittance|settlement|clearing|BPAY|NPP|BECS|RTGS|direct.?debit|direct.?credit' applied to ctrl_name + ctrl_description concatenated). Output first-pass JUNO payment control population with paths fired, primary path, confidence rollup. Also produce taxonomy hygiene finding: proportion of payment controls included via paths other than P1 (if >40% are non-P1, indicates taxonomy misclassification or incomplete tagging; reportable to sponsor as data quality issue).
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Four deterministic paths execute against full JUNO universe via Teradata pass-through (run 02_code/sql/teradata_passthrough/step04_p1_taxonomy.sql, step04_p3_obligation.sql, step04_p4_incident_issue.sql, step04_p5_keyword.sql; materialise results to SAS via 02_code/sas/step04_control_inclusion.sas): P1 WHERE risk_library_id LIKE '7.4.%', P3 join linkage_ctrl_oblig → obligations WHERE obligation_source IN (...), P4 join linkage_ctrl_incident → incidents WHERE incident linked to 7.4.x control OR payment process (defer full logic to step 6 Pass 2+; Pass 1 uses 7.4.x only), P5 WHERE ctrl_name || ' ' || ctrl_description ~* 'payment|payor|...' (Teradata regex syntax)
2. Output dataset created: 03_data/intermediate/step04_juno_payment_controls.sas7bdat with schema: ctrl_id, ctrl_name, ctrl_description, owner_business_unit, control_type, automation_level, effectiveness_rating, p1_fired, p2_fired (initially NULL), p3_fired, p4_fired, p5_fired, p6_fired (initially NULL), primary_path, confidence_rollup
3. Taxonomy hygiene finding produced: count controls by primary_path; compute % with primary_path != 'P1'; if >40%, flag as taxonomy hygiene issue; output to 00_documentation/taxonomy_hygiene_finding.md with breakdown: total payment controls, count per path, % per path, recommendation (if P1 <60%, recommend taxonomy review and re-tagging initiative post-PoC)
4. Audit log created: 05_audit_trail/audit_trail_step04_deterministic.csv with every JUNO CTRL_ID: ctrl_id, p1_result, p3_result, p4_result, p5_result, inclusion_decision, confidence, primary_path, reason_if_excluded

Description: Compute embeddings for all JUNO control descriptions (concatenate ctrl_name + ctrl_description for embedding input). Save to 04_embeddings/juno_control_embeddings.npy with index 04_embeddings/embedding_index_juno.csv. P6 similarity: identify high-confidence core (controls with P1, P2, or P3 fired; confidence=High), compute centroid, compute cosine similarity of all other controls to centroid, calibrate threshold via golden set from PRS-44 (SME-labelled ~50 controls; measure precision/recall at thresholds; select threshold achieving precision ≥0.75, recall ≥0.70). Enrichment signals (used ONLY for SME queue prioritisation, NOT for inclusion): owner clustering (if business unit has ≥80% of its controls already included via P1–P3, flag remaining controls from that BU as higher priority for SME review), process-adjacency (controls owned by same BU or operating on same system/application as already-linked controls but not themselves linked; flag as higher priority). Enrichment signals scored 0–100; SME queue ordered by score descending. Candidate controls above P6 similarity threshold written to SME queue for review (NOT auto-included).
Acceptance Criteria:
1. JUNO embeddings generated: run 02_code/python/step04_p6_embedding.py which reads 03_data/staging/juno_staging.sas7bdat, concatenates ctrl_name + ' | ' + ctrl_description per row, calls embedding_service.compute_embeddings(), saves to 04_embeddings/juno_control_embeddings.npy and 04_embeddings/embedding_index_juno.csv
2. P6 similarity computed: identify high-conf core (controls with p1_fired=TRUE OR p2_fired=TRUE OR p3_fired=TRUE; expect 800–2000 controls), compute centroid embedding, compute cosine similarity of all non-core controls to centroid, calibrate threshold using golden set from PRS-44 (plot precision/recall vs threshold; select threshold where precision ≥0.75 AND recall ≥0.70; document in 03_data/validation/p6_threshold_calibration.csv)
3. (b) Process-adjacency: for each non-included control, check if owner_business_unit OR linked_application matches any already-included control; if match, enrichment_score += 30. Description: Build fuzzy matcher for step 5 bespoke control discovery. Fuzzy matcher compares candidate bespoke control text (from Holocentric steps, ALEX configs, or remediation text) against JUNO control descriptions to detect if the control is already registered under different wording. Use token-based similarity: Levenshtein distance, Jaccard similarity on word n-grams (n=2,3), or TF-IDF cosine similarity. Calibrate threshold on known-duplicate sample: select 20 JUNO controls, manually rewrite descriptions with paraphrasing, run fuzzy matcher, measure recall (should be 100% on exact semantic duplicates) and precision (false positive rate <5% on non-duplicates). Threshold set to ≥0.80 similarity = likely same control (flag as already registered). Lower similarity 0.60–0.79 = possible duplicate (queue to SME for adjudication). Below 0.60 = distinct control (candidate bespoke). Fuzzy matcher used in PRS-14, PRS-15, PRS-16.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Fuzzy matcher implemented in 02_code/python/llm_orchestration/fuzzy_matching.py with function fuzzy_match(candidate_text, juno_controls_df, threshold=0.80) returning (best_match_ctrl_id, similarity_score, match_decision = 'Already_Registered' / 'Possible_Duplicate' / 'Distinct'); use Jaccard similarity on word bigrams + trigrams (average the two scores) or rapidfuzz library for Levenshtein ratio
2. Threshold calibrated on known-duplicate sample: manually create test set of 20 JUNO controls with paraphrased descriptions (e.g., "Daily reconciliation of payment files" → "Reconcile payment transactions on a daily basis"), run fuzzy_match() with thresholds 0.70, 0.75, 0.80, 0.85, measure recall (% of paraphrases correctly matched to original; target 100% at threshold 0.80), measure precision on non-duplicate set (20 controls from different CTs/processes; false positive rate <5% at threshold 0.80)
3. Threshold documented: selected threshold (recommend 0.80) saved to 02_code/python/llm_orchestration/config.py as FUZZY_MATCH_THRESHOLD; calibration results saved to 00_documentation/fuzzy_match_calibration.csv with columns: threshold, recall, precision, false_positive_rate, false_negative_rate
4. Integration tested: run fuzzy_match() on 10 known bespoke controls (from prior risk assessments or SME nominations) against JUNO; verify Already_Registered decisions are correct (controls that should be in JUNO are flagged), verify Distinct decisions are correct (genuinely new controls are not falsely matched)

Description: Orchestrate steps 2 and 4 alternately until both populations stabilise (no new High or Medium confidence items added in consecutive passes). Convergence safeguard: only High-confidence inclusions propagate via PP4 (process linked to High-confidence control from step 4) and P2 (control linked to High-confidence process from step 2). Medium-confidence may propagate but with confidence ceiling (inherited inclusion cannot be rated higher than source; Medium source → Medium inherited, never High). Low-confidence (PP5/P5 keyword-only, PP6/P6 embedding-only) does NOT propagate until cleared from Requires Human Review queue by SME. This prevents amplification of low-confidence noise across iterations. Loop logic: Pass 1 runs steps 2 and 4 with PP4 and P2 disabled. Pass 2 re-runs step 2 with PP4 enabled (reads High-confidence controls from step 4 Pass 1, joins via linkage_ctrl_proc, fires PP4 for linked processes), re-runs step 4 with P2 enabled (reads High-confidence processes from step 2 Pass 2, joins via linkage_ctrl_proc, fires P2 for linked controls). Continue until convergence (zero new H/M items) or hard cap of 5 passes. Typical convergence: 2–3 passes. Log pass-by-pass deltas to measure mutual contribution.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Orchestrator implemented: 02_code/sas/step06_convergence_loop.sas with loop structure: Pass 1 = run step02_process_inclusion.sas (PP1/PP2/PP3/PP5 only; PP4 disabled), run step04_control_inclusion.sas (P1/P3/P4/P5 only; P2 disabled); Pass 2+ = run step02 with PP4 enabled (read step04_juno_payment_controls where confidence='High', join to linkage_ctrl_proc, fire PP4 for matched processes; update step02_payment_process_register.pp4_fired and recalc confidence_rollup), run step04 with P2 enabled (read step02_payment_process_register where confidence='High', join to linkage_ctrl_proc, fire P2 for matched controls; update step04_juno_payment_controls.p2_fired and recalc confidence_rollup); repeat until convergence
2. Confidence ceiling enforced: if process inherited via PP4 from Medium-confidence control, process confidence capped at Medium (cannot be High); if control inherited via P2 from Medium-confidence process, control confidence capped at Medium; implemented in confidence_rollup recalc logic
3. Pass-by-pass delta log written: 03_data/intermediate/step06_convergence_deltas.sas7bdat with schema: pass_number, step_name (step2/step4), items_added_high, items_added_medium, items_added_low, total_population_size_after_pass; compute delta = items_added this pass; convergence achieved when items_added_high=0 AND items_added_medium=0 for both steps in same pass
4. Convergence criteria: loop terminates when (items_added_high=0 AND items_added_medium=0 for step2 in pass N) AND (items_added_high=0 AND items_added_medium=0 for step4 in pass N); OR pass_number=5 (hard cap); if hard cap reached without convergence, log residual delta and flag for manual review in 00_documentation/convergence_manual_review.md; typical result: convergence in pass 2 or 3 with <5% population growth per pass after pass 2

Description: Place every control at its payment lifecycle stage (A Initiation through G Returns and Recoveries). Hybrid method: structural placement where derivable from Holocentric process step labels, LLM placement as primary otherwise, misplacement detection only where both exist and can be compared. Structural placement (9a): where Holocentric process steps carry explicit stage labels (e.g., step_name contains 'Validation', 'Authorisation', 'Settlement', 'Reconciliation', 'Notification', 'Returns'), map directly to lifecycle stages A–G. For controls linked to labelled step, structural-expected stage is derived (expect 30–60% coverage depending on Holocentric labelling consistency; measured in PRS-3). LLM placement (9b): LLM runs on all controls (can be combined with step 8 call; single prompt emits both CT mappings and lifecycle stage to reduce API call volume). For controls with structural-expected stage, LLM placement is compared to structural expectation. Disagreement is quality signal: (a) LLM wrong, (b) Holocentric step mislabelled, OR (c) control operates at different stage than linked step suggests (genuine misplacement finding for step 11e gap register). Misplacement detection only possible where structural-expected exists AND differs from LLM; absence of structural-expected means LLM placement recorded but no misplacement assertion can be made.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Structural placement derived: join unified_controls to linkage_ctrl_proc to get linked process_ids, join to Holocentric step-level detail, extract step_name and step_description, apply regex mapping: IF step_name CONTAINS 'initiat|onboard|request|origination' → structural_expected_stage='A Initiation', IF CONTAINS 'validat|verif|authori|approv|dual.?control' → 'B Validation and Authentication', IF CONTAINS 'release|submit|transmit' → 'C Release into Processing', IF CONTAINS 'clear|settle|RTGS|BECS|NPP' → 'D Clearing and Settlement', IF CONTAINS 'post|ledger|account.?update' → 'E Posting to Accounts', IF CONTAINS 'notif|report|confirm|advice' → 'F Notification and Reporting', IF CONTAINS 'return|revers|recall|recover|dispute|chargeback' → 'G Returns and Recoveries'; controls with no match OR no linked Holocentric step receive structural_expected_stage=NULL (expect 40–70% NULL)
2. LLM placement runs: for each control, call LLM (recommend combined with step 8 call for efficiency; single prompt emits ct_mappings + lifecycle_stage; else separate call with prompt 01_prompts/step09_lifecycle_placement.txt), input = {control_id, control_name, control_description, control_type, payment_nature, linked_process_names, structural_expected_stage (if exists; passed as hint but LLM classifies independently)}, parse JSON {lifecycle_stage: enum[A Initiation, B Validation and Authentication, C Release into Processing, D Clearing and Settlement, E Posting to Accounts, F Notification and Reporting, G Returns and Recoveries], confidence: enum[H, M, L], rationale}; run via 02_code/python/step09_lifecycle.py OR combined with step08_ct_mapping.py
3. Structural check performed: for each control, compare llm_lifecycle_stage to structural_expected_stage; IF both exist AND differ → structural_check='Mismatch', misplacement_candidate=TRUE, queue to SME for adjudication (could be LLM wrong, Holocentric label wrong, or genuine control misplacement); IF structural_expected_stage=NULL → structural_check='Not-derivable', misplacement_candidate=FALSE (honest scoping: cannot assert misplacement without structural reference); IF both exist AND match → structural_check='Match', confidence boosted to High
4. Output dataset created: 03_data/intermediate/step09_control_lifecycle.sas7bdat with schema: control_id, lifecycle_stage (LLM result), lifecycle_confidence, structural_expected_stage, structural_check (Match/Mismatch/Not-derivable), misplacement_candidate_flag, lifecycle_rationale, prompt_version_hash, model_id, run_timestamp; misplacement candidates (structural_check='Mismatch') written to 06_sme_review/sme_queue_step09_misplacement.xlsx for adjudication; validation gate from PRS-45: golden set ~50 controls (same as step 8); target: exact-match accuracy ≥0.80; if met, scale; if not, iterate

Summary: Implement step 10: Build master bridge table
Description: Compose all upstream outputs (steps 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9) into a single analytical table. Bridge is the master data model: every analytical output in step 11 queries this table. Pure SAS assembly, no LLM at this step. Joins are deterministic. Bridge row schema (one row per process × control × CT × Payment Nature × lifecycle stage intersection): process_id, process_name, process_value_stream, process_applications; control_id, control_name, control_description, control_source (JUNO/bespoke-Holocentric/bespoke-ALEX/bespoke-remediation), registration_status (Registered if JUNO, Candidate if bespoke not SME-confirmed, Confirmed-unregistered if bespoke SME-confirmed); ct_outcome (CT1–CT28), ct_confidence, ct_rationale, ct_match_type; control_category (Process/System/Third-Party/Pervasive), control_nature (Preventative/Detective/Corrective), framework_alignment (Payments/Governance); payment_nature, nature_inherent_risk (High/Medium/Low from Payment Nature definition), nature_source (Inherited/LLM-fallback); lifecycle_stage, lifecycle_confidence, structural_check; design_effectiveness, operating_effectiveness, overall_effectiveness (from JUNO ratings); incident_count_linked, issue_count_linked, latest_incident_severity, latest_incident_date; provenance (prompt_version_hash, model_id, run_timestamp from steps 8/9 primarily). Indexed on five filter dimensions: ct_outcome, payment_nature, lifecycle_stage, control_category, process_value_stream for query performance.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Bridge join logic implemented in 02_code/sas/step10_build_bridge.sas: (a) Start with step08_control_ct_mapping (one row per control per CT) as base, (b) LEFT JOIN to step07_control_payment_nature ON control_id (one-to-many; control with 2 natures becomes 2 rows per CT), (c) LEFT JOIN to step09_control_lifecycle ON control_id, (d) LEFT JOIN to unified_controls (JUNO + bespoke) to get control_name/description/source/owner/type/automation/effectiveness ratings, (e) LEFT JOIN to linkage_ctrl_proc to get linked process_ids, (f) LEFT JOIN to step02_payment_process_register and step03_process_payment_nature to get process details, (g) LEFT JOIN to linkage_ctrl_incident/linkage_ctrl_issue to aggregate incident_count, issue_count, latest_incident_severity/date per control, (h) Final schema per runbook with all fields documented above
2. Indexes created for query performance: CREATE INDEX idx_ct ON bridge_table (ct_outcome), CREATE INDEX idx_nature ON bridge_table (payment_nature), CREATE INDEX idx_stage ON bridge_table (lifecycle_stage), CREATE INDEX idx_category ON bridge_table (control_category), CREATE INDEX idx_valuestream ON bridge_table (process_value_stream); SAS syntax: PROC DATASETS; MODIFY bridge_table; INDEX CREATE idx_ct / UNIQUE; etc.
3. Output dataset created: 03_data/intermediate/step10_bridge_table.sas7bdat; row count reconciliation: total bridge rows should equal sum across controls of (count_CTs_per_control × count_Natures_per_control); spot-check: select 10 controls, manually count expected bridge rows (if control has 3 CTs and 2 natures, expect 6 bridge rows), compare to actual; verify 100% match
4. Documentation: every bridge column source documented in 00_documentation/bridge_table_schema.md with column_name, data_type, source_step, source_dataset, join_key, null_handling, example_values; lead engineer review and sign-off before step 11 begins

Description: Generate three coverage heatmaps (Payment Nature × CT, Value Stream × CT, Process × CT), each showing three coverage constructs per cell: Structural (control exists and mapped to CT for this Nature/ValueStream/Process), Effective (Structural AND control rated Effective in overall_effectiveness from JUNO), Failing (Structural AND rated Effective BUT linked incidents/issues contradict the rating; method-failure indicator). Query bridge table with GROUP BY on dimension pairs. Cell with 5 Structural / 4 Effective / 1 Failing tells different story than 1 Structural / 1 Effective / 0 Failing; three numbers preserve this distinction. Export to Excel with conditional formatting: green cells (Effective ≥3 AND Failing=0), amber (Effective 1–2 OR Failing >0), red (Structural=0 no coverage). These are the primary sufficiency finding for sponsor.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Payment Nature × CT heatmap: query bridge_table GROUP BY payment_nature, ct_outcome; for each cell compute: structural_count = COUNT(DISTINCT control_id), effective_count = COUNT(DISTINCT control_id WHERE overall_effectiveness='Effective'), failing_count = COUNT(DISTINCT control_id WHERE overall_effectiveness='Effective' AND (incident_count_linked >0 OR issue_count_linked >0) AND latest_incident_date > today()-730 days); output to 03_data/outputs/11a_coverage_heatmap_nature_ct.xlsx with rows=Payment Nature (5 rows: C→C, I→C, C→I, I→I, Supplier/Employee), columns=CT (28 columns: CT1–CT28), cell_value=Structural / Effective / Failing (formatted as "5 / 4 / 1")
2. Value Stream × CT heatmap: same query logic GROUP BY process_value_stream, ct_outcome; output to 03_data/outputs/11a_coverage_heatmap_valuestream_ct.xlsx; rows=distinct value_streams from Holocentric (expect 8–12 value streams), columns=CT1–CT28
3. Process × CT heatmap: same query logic GROUP BY process_name, ct_outcome (WARNING: large matrix; expect 200–500 processes × 28 CTs = 5,600–14,000 cells; Excel row limit 1,048,576 so safe); output to 03_data/outputs/11a_coverage_heatmap_process_ct.xlsx for granular view by control owners
4. Conditional formatting applied in Excel export: SAS ODS EXCEL with STYLE statement or post-export VBA macro; green fill if effective_count ≥3 AND failing_count=0, amber fill if effective_count 1–2 OR failing_count >0, red fill if structural_count=0; run 02_code/sas/step11a_coverage_heatmaps.sas to generate all three files

Description: Highlight controls with strong sufficiency characteristics: automated controls in High inherent risk Payment Natures (C→C, I→C), preventative controls at critical lifecycle stages (A Initiation, B Validation and Authentication, C Release into Processing where prevention most valuable), controls rated Effective with zero P1/P2 incidents in last 24 months (candidate exemplars for best-practice sharing). Query bridge table with filters. Output used by control owners to identify and amplify existing strong controls.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Automated controls in High-risk natures extracted: query bridge_table WHERE payment_nature IN ('C→C', 'I→C') AND (automation_level='Automated' OR control_type='Automated') AND overall_effectiveness='Effective'; output columns: control_id, control_name, payment_nature, ct_outcome, lifecycle_stage, owner_business_unit, automation_level, incident_count_linked, issue_count_linked; save to strengthen_view_automated_high_risk subset
2. Preventative controls at critical stages extracted: query bridge_table WHERE control_nature='Preventative' AND lifecycle_stage IN ('A Initiation', 'B Validation and Authentication', 'C Release into Processing') AND overall_effectiveness IN ('Effective', 'Largely Effective'); output same columns; save to strengthen_view_preventative_early_stage subset
3. Exemplar candidates extracted: query bridge_table WHERE overall_effectiveness='Effective' AND incident_count_linked=0 AND issue_count_linked=0 AND (SELECT MAX(incident_date) FROM incidents WHERE ctrl_id=bridge.control_id) < today()-730 OR incident_date IS NULL (no incidents in 24 months); add flag exemplar_candidate=TRUE with rationale="Effective rating + incident-free 24mo history"
4. Output consolidated: UNION all three subsets (automated-high-risk, preventative-early, exemplar) with subset_type flag; export to 03_data/outputs/11b_strengthen_view.xlsx with sheets per subset type; run 02_code/sas/step11b_strengthen_view.sas

Summary: Produce step 11c: Duplicate clusters and best of breed
Description: Identify duplicate clusters: controls sharing (CT outcome AND Payment Nature AND lifecycle stage AND process scope) with mechanism similarity ≥0.75 (cosine of control description + automation level + control type embeddings; automation matters: automated check + manual reconciliation covering same CT/Nature/Stage are NOT duplicates, they are defence-in-depth). Score each cluster member via five-factor formula: 0.40×effectiveness + 0.25×automation + 0.20×incident-free history + 0.10×design clarity + 0.05×coverage breadth; highest score = best of breed nomination, others = retire/merge candidates. Weights are sponsor-tunable (formula structure fixed, weights adjustable post first-cut results). Effectiveness score: Effective=100, Largely Effective=75, Requires Improvement=40, Ineffective=0. Automation: Automated=100, Hybrid=60, Manual=30, Unknown=0. Incident-free: 100 if zero P1/P2 in 24mo, decrease by severity and recency (P1 recent = -50 points). Design clarity: LLM-scored once on description token length + structural completeness. Coverage breadth: % of cluster's process scope covered by this control.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Clustering logic: for each unique combination of (ct_outcome, payment_nature, lifecycle_stage), extract controls from bridge_table; within each combo group, compute pairwise mechanism similarity using control description embeddings (from step 8/9; if not saved, re-compute via embedding_service), automation_level (encoded as one-hot vector: Automated=[1,0,0], Hybrid=[0,1,0], Manual=[0,0,1]), control_type (encoded similarly); concatenate vectors, compute cosine similarity; IF similarity ≥0.75 AND automation_level differs → NOT duplicate (defence-in-depth); IF similarity ≥0.75 AND automation_level same → duplicate cluster; output cluster_id per control
2. Best-of-breed scoring: for each control in a cluster, compute: effectiveness_score = CASE overall_effectiveness WHEN 'Effective' THEN 100 WHEN 'Largely Effective' THEN 75 WHEN 'Requires Improvement' THEN 40 ELSE 0, automation_score = CASE automation_level WHEN 'Automated' THEN 100 WHEN 'Hybrid' THEN 60 WHEN 'Manual' THEN 30 ELSE 0, incident_free_score = 100 - (incident_count_linked_P1_24mo × 50) - (incident_count_linked_P2_24mo × 25) capped at 0, design_clarity_score = LLM-scored 0–100 on description completeness (run once per control; store in bridge or separate dataset), coverage_breadth_score = (count distinct processes this control linked to / count distinct processes in cluster) × 100; total_score = 0.40×effectiveness + 0.25×automation + 0.20×incident_free + 0.10×design_clarity + 0.05×coverage_breadth; within each cluster, rank by total_score descending; rank 1 = best_of_breed, rank >1 = retire/merge candidate
3. Output dataset: one row per control in a duplicate cluster: cluster_id, control_id, control_name, ct_outcome, payment_nature, lifecycle_stage, mechanism_similarity_to_cluster_centroid, effectiveness_score, automation_score, incident_free_score, design_clarity_score, coverage_breadth_score, total_score, rank_in_cluster, best_of_breed_flag, recommendation (Best-of-breed/Retire/Merge); export to 03_data/outputs/11c_duplicate_clusters.xlsx; run 02_code/sas/step11c_duplicates_best_of_breed.sas
4. Sponsor tuning: weights (0.40/0.25/0.20/0.10/0.05) stored in config file; if sponsor requests weight adjustment after first-cut review, update config and re-run scoring (formula structure unchanged)

These controls address governance/framework operation (policy authorship, committee oversight, training, framework compliance) rather than direct payment risk mitigation. Specifically requested by sponsor in project deck.

3. Output format: control_id, control_name, control_description (truncated to 200 chars for readability), owner_business_unit, current_risk_library_id (7.4.x tag), framework_alignment_flag='Governance', governance_rationale (from step 8), recommendation="Remove from Payments Risk framework; re-home under Governance/Operational Risk", priority (High if key_control_flag=TRUE, else Medium); export to 03_data/outputs/11d_governance_misclassified.xlsx
